summary.prose: Calls made in a file's top-level statements are recorded, credited to the file itself. Every test written as test('…', () => { … }) is such a statement, so after this change a test file's calls reach the functions they exercise, and the code review's test links reflect real tests.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

boundary.internal: Record calls made in module-level statements, so tests reach the code they call

api.name: walkNode
api.signature: walkNode(node: SyntaxNode, source: string, repo: string, repoId: number, filePath: string, lang: Language, fileId: string, now: string, entities: Entity[], relations: Relation[]): void

parameters.name: node
parameters.purpose: The node being walked; module-level handling applies when node.parent is the program node.

parameters.name: fileId
parameters.purpose: The file entity id, now also the caller of module-level calls.

postconditions: For a program-level expression_statement, extractCalls runs over the statement with fileId as the caller, then the walk into its children continues as today.

For a program-level lexical_declaration or variable_declaration, each declarator whose value is not an arrow_function, function_expression or generator_function_expression has extractCalls run over its value with fileId as the caller; function-valued declarators are unchanged (extractArrowFunction).
For any other program-level statement that is not a declaration walkNode already handles (if/for/while/try/block/labeled statements), extractCalls runs over it with fileId as the caller.
Calls inside function declarations, class bodies and function-valued declarators are not also credited to the file, unless they are nested inside a module-level statement.

api.name: extractCalls
api.signature: extractCalls(bodyNode: SyntaxNode, callerId: string, repo: string, filePath: string, relations: Relation[]): void

parameters.name: callerId
parameters.purpose: Now also the file entity id for module-level calls.

returns.meaning: Unchanged: CALLS (and CALLS_HTTP) relations from callerId.

dataModelChanges.details: A CALLS (or CALLS_HTTP) relation may now have the file entity as its source, for calls in module-level statements. No new entity kind, no new field, no store schema change.

errorCases.scenario: A file is re-indexed or deleted after module-level calls were recorded from its file entity.
errorCases.detection: indexFile and fileEvent delete the file's entities (src/indexer/index.ts:1041, :785); the entity cascade removes incident edges and deleteUnresolvedForFile removes the file's pending CALLS rows.
errorCases.response: Nothing new: the file entity is deleted with the file, so its CALLS go with it; the re-parse emits the current ones.

edgeCases.expected: One CALLS foo from the file entity (nested callbacks are walked).

edgeCases.input: const deps = makeDeps(); at program level
edgeCases.expected: CALLS makeDeps from the file entity.

edgeCases.input: const f = () => bar(); at program level
edgeCases.expected: Unchanged: an entity f with CALLS bar from f; not also from the file.
Unchanged: CALLS baz from g only.
helper is an entity with CALLS qux (as today); the file entity also calls qux and helper, because both are inside the module-level statement.

edgeCases.input: A module-level call to console.log or another built-in
edgeCases.expected: Skipped by the existing built-in filter, as inside functions.
An export_statement with a value is treated as a module-level statement: CALLS foo from the file entity.
A CALLS_HTTP from the file entity, as the HTTP recognizer already does inside functions.

invariantsToPreserve.text: Calls inside function declarations, class methods and function-valued declarators keep their current caller and are not duplicated onto the file.
A file's edges are removed with its entities on re-index or delete; module-level CALLS from the file entity must follow the same clean-up.
The code review counts a caller as a test caller by its file (isTestFile).

testStrategy.testFramework: node:test via npx tsx --test (assert/strict), run under Node 22

migration.stateBefore: Per s1: the TypeScript parser extracts calls only inside function declarations, class methods and function-valued declarators (src/indexer/parser/typescript.ts:259, :419, :552); calls in program-level statements are never recorded, so no test file reaches any symbol.
migration.stateAfter: Calls in program-level statements are CALLS (or CALLS_HTTP) from the file entity; existing attribution is unchanged.

migrationSteps.action: Add the module-level handling to walkNode.
Update and restart the installed daemon, then reindex the repositories (or let the watcher re-parse changed files) so existing files gain their module-level CALLS.

migration.backwardCompat: No store schema change and no new entity kind. Until a file is re-parsed it keeps its old edges, so a full reindex is needed for complete test links.

alternativesConsidered.name: Credit module-level calls to the file entity
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: A call in a program-level statement that is not a declaration, or in a program-level non-function initializer, is emitted as CALLS from the file entity.
alternativesConsidered.approach: walkNode gains a case for a program-level expression_statement (and any other program-level statement that is not a declaration the walker already handles) and for a program-level const/let whose value is not a function: extractCalls runs over it with the file entity as the caller. The walk into its children continues as today, so nested named declarations still become entities with their own CALLS. No new entity kind and no store change; the file entity already exists, is a test file's entity for test files, and is deleted with the file.
pros: No schema or EntityKind change; reuses the file entity and the existing cascade clean-up.
Meets the fix intent: a test file's calls reach the symbols it exercises, and the review joins them to the record per file (ISSUE-1102dc71).
cons: Test-level granularity is lost: the caller is the test file, not the test title.
Calls inside a nested named helper are credited both to the helper and to the file.

alternativesConsidered.name: A synthetic entity per top-level test call
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Each test('title', ...) / it(...) at program level becomes an entity named by its title that owns the calls in its callback.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Recognise test-runner calls (test, it, describe and their variants) at program level, create an entity per call named by its title, and credit the callback's calls to it; other module-level calls go to the file entity.
pros: Test-title granularity: a caller names the very test that reaches a symbol.
cons: A new EntityKind needs its byte mapping in the graph keys and a store schema step (the live store is v5).
Runner recognition is heuristic and per framework; titles can be computed strings.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Adds a new EntityKind and a store schema step on the live v5 store for test-title granularity the code review does not use (it joins callers to the test record per file).

alternativesConsidered.name: File-entity credit for test files only
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: As a1, but only in files isTestFile matches.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Same mechanism as a1, guarded by the test-file predicate.
cons: Production module-level calls (top-level registration, setup) stay invisible to "who calls this".
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Partial on fixIntent-1: production module-level calls stay unrecorded.

openQuestions: ts1 (partial): the standalone story carries no acceptance criteria; the test strategy maps two derived from the approved issue's fix intent (ac1 module-level calls are CALLS from the file entity, ac2 a test file reaches the symbols it calls in the code-review grounding) [c6].
Kotlin and Scala DSL-style tests written in a class body (test("x") { ... }) were not checked; out of scope here [c4].
